translations.en: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, al-Misami, Abu Muhammad.

chunks.arabic_text: ضَعِيفٌ، مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ. لَهُ كِتَابٌ فِي الزِّيَارَاتِ، مَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى خَبْثٍ عَظِيمٍ، وَمَذْهَبٌ مُتَهَافِتٌ. وَكَانَ مِنْ كَذَّابَةِ أَهْلِ الْبَصْرَةِ.

translations.en: Weak, a proponent of irtifa' in doctrine. He has a book about ziyarat, what gives evidence of his great filth and collapsed madhhab. He was from liars of the people of Basra.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā’* critiques ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aṣamm, a Basran narrator known for *irtifāʿ al-qawl* (elevating the status of his reports), for his distinctively Shia-leaning yet flawed *ziyārat* literature. His work is characterized by 'great filth' (*khabth ʿazīm*) and a 'collapsed school of thought' (*madhhab mutahāfat*), reflecting the rigorous scrutiny of early Shia hadith scholars who valued doctrinal purity alongside narrative accuracy. This critique highlights the tension in Basra between emerging Shia devotional practices and the established standards of *rijāl* (biographical evaluation).
en.seo_question: Who is Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ: Proponent of irtifa' (raising the status of a narration)
key_terms.خَبْثٍ عَظِيمٍ: Great filth (metaphorical for deep flaw or impurity in thought/text)
